accounts.prose: This module is the package façade: it implements no merge logic, but wildcard-re-exports the merge API and the array-concatenation helper. Its public surface is `merge`, `mergeAndCompare`, `mergeAndConcat`, `concatArrays`, and the type-only `Merge`.
qualifications: Interpretation of captured TypeScript source and compiler export records; execution, packaging, and loader behavior were not tested.

accounts.prose: The exported `Merge<T, Ts>` models the runtime result separately from runtime execution. If the first value and all later values are record-like, `Assign` walks the tuple and delegates each pair to `MergeDeep`; that type recursively combines record-valued fields while accounting for required and optional keys. `PrettyPrint` expands the resulting intersections with cycle detection. If those record constraints fail, `Pop` selects the final argument type instead.

referent.description: compile-time return-type calculation used by the merge functions

qualifications: This is TypeScript type-level behavior, not runtime validation.
The deeper iteration helper used by `Assign` was identified but not read; the captured `Assign` source was sufficient to establish tuple traversal and delegation.

accounts.prose: `concatArrays` is a narrow merge policy: when both old and incoming values are arrays it returns their concatenation; otherwise the incoming value wins. It is both directly public and used by `mergeAndConcat`.
qualifications: Static source interpretation; array detection is delegated to uninspected `is-what` code.

qualifications: External dependency supplies array detection; its implementation was not acquired.

accounts.prose: The merge implementation folds later arguments left-to-right. Each step returns a non-plain incoming value directly; otherwise it builds a fresh plain object, preserves origin keys absent from the newcomer, and recursively combines overlapping values only when the incoming value is plain. It includes string and symbol own-property names, preserves enumerable versus non-enumerable status but recreates descriptors as writable/configurable data properties, and drops `__proto__`. `mergeAndCompare` applies a caller callback to every incoming property after any recursion; `mergeAndConcat` supplies the array helper as that callback. Plain-object and symbol classification is delegated to `is-what`.

referent.description: runtime recursive merge implementation and three public merge variants

qualifications: Static reading only; `is-what` internals and runtime behavior were not inspected.

The nearby README says merge always returns a new object, but with no later arguments the implementation's reduction returns the original first argument; it also describes the comparison callback as firing on overwrite, whereas the implementation invokes it for every incoming property, including one without an origin value.
